- When sentiment is positive (≥ 0.20) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If model shows sharp upward spike in forecast (e.g., >10% from prior day), it often overshoots; cap forecast at 1–2% above prior peak.  
- If history shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of downward trend), model often fails to correct; adjust forecast to align with 30-day moving average.  
- When sentiment is negative (≤ -0.15) and price is falling, model often underestimates; add 1–2% to forecast to avoid premature bottoming.  
- For 30-day horizon, model frequently underestimates in early days of a downtrend; apply slight upward bias (0.5–1.5%) for first 5–7 days.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated positive spikes followed by negative sentiment, model tends to lag; delay forecast correction by 1–2 days.
